brief: A wall clock with hands that turn and tell the time.
costSource: token-equivalent at Muse Spark Open shared rates, info only: the Dedicated Endpoint bills GPU seconds while up (.spend/modal-dedicated.jsonl)

requirements.requirement: Wall clock - large flat face suitable to hang on wall
requirements.evidence: 7 x full hex bases with covers creating 453x475mm flat disc (covers 0,0,0 etc) - shows as clock face but has no hanging hardware; Hex Cluster is desk/shelf system with no wall-mount parts

No movement mechanism exists in catalog; configurator only checks fit/collision, knows nothing about mechanics. Hands represented by static props: ruler (long hand) and pencil (short hand) on cover:0,0,0;full;top - they do not turn
Parts are 3D-printed plastic only; no clock motor, electronics, or timekeeping capability in Hex Cluster. Cannot meet.

finish.summary: Built a 7-hex decorative clock face (wall-clock shape) with static hand props (ruler + pencil) to suggest hands, but true turning hands and timekeeping are impossible: the system provides only static 3D-printed structural parts with no motors, electronics, or moving mechanism, and no wall-mount hardware.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
